post.summary: Decide an approval outside the socket (notification actions, the watch)
post.description: Replaces POST /v1/approvals/{id} for decisions. The body is ApprovalResume in its camelCase (keyId), as in a socket resume. A cancelled answer is not sent here: cancelling decides nothing, and the approval stays pending until decided elsewhere or expired. Header X-Pisa-Origin: notification when sent from a notification action. CONTRACT-2 §6.1.

200.description: The resuming run, collected: pisa.action_done, or RUN_ERROR with approval_changed, approval_expired, approval_decided, biometric_required or action_failed (approved, ran, failed).

post.summary: A single-use nonce, and the canonical text the phone signs after Face ID
post.description:
The approval challenge gains interrupt_id and returns the pisa-approval/2 canonical text. The device challenge's canonical becomes pisa-device: 'pisa-device
op=<op>
target=<target>
nonce=<nonce>
expires_at=<iso>' (v1's j-device with the prefix renamed), and its op enum gains model_server. The signed request carries X-Pisa-Nonce, X-Pisa-Signature (DER, base64) and X-Pisa-Key-Id.

put.summary: How notices reach this device: the relay, direct APNs, or none
put.description: Relay mode added (CONTRACT-2 §9). The server deletes a relay registration when the relay answers 404 or 410 (the handle is gone); a 422 to a liveactivity push drops only that activity's token, and the registration stays.

delete.summary: Unpair: revoke this device's keys, push and Live Activity registrations
delete.description: CONTRACT-2 §4.5. Afterwards this device's next connect gets device_revoked.

post.summary: Begin pairing: the server commits to its nonce before seeing the app's transcript
post.description: No auth and no token: it only commits. Rate-limited per client address. The app keeps the commitment and checks the serverNonce that POST /v1/pair reveals against it. CONTRACT-2 §4.3, §15 S1.

201.description: The pairing id and the commitment.

post.summary: Pair with the QR token (HMAC transcript, then SAS on the server side)
post.description: Replaces POST /v1/devices/pair. 400 pairing_code_invalid when the mac matches no open token. Such a request names no token, so it counts only toward an address backstop (IPv6 /64 or IPv4, much higher than 5) and never retires a token or locks out an address (E1 P2). The token is protected by its 128 bits, single use, a 10-minute expiry and at most 5 open tokens. Carries the pairingId from POST /v1/pair/begin; the answer reveals serverNonce, which the app checks against the commitment before showing the SAS (a mismatch aborts pairing; the token stays spent). CONTRACT-2 §4.3.

201.description: Awaiting the user's confirmation on the server side.

get.summary: A nonce for the device key to sign
get.description: Single use (60 s), consumed whether or not the session request succeeds. Bound (deviceId): at most 5 outstanding per device. Unbound: at most 5 per client address (the IPv6 /64 or the IPv4 address, from X-Forwarded-For only behind a trusted proxy), and a server-wide cap (reference value 10 000). 429 rate_limited past either.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The device the nonce is for. The app always sends it (E1 P2): a bound nonce opens a session for that device only, at most 5 outstanding per device.

post.summary: A short-lived (1 h) session token from the device key's signature
post.description: Replaces v1's never-expiring device token. The device key signs 'pisa-session/1\n<deviceId>\n<nonce>' (ECDSA P-256 SHA-256, DER, base64). On expiry REST answers 401 session_expired and /v2/live closes with 4003 and the reason session_expired (no control frame): the app signs a new nonce. /v2/live and /v2/runs take a session token only. CONTRACT-2 §4.3; vectors fixtures/pairing/vectors.json.

token.description: Opaque, 32 random bytes; the server stores only its SHA-256.

post.summary: A paired phone offers to pair a new device: it shows the QR
post.description: Replaces v1's pairing-code path (POST /v1/devices/pairing-code). Signed: device op pairing_offer, target '<SHA-256 hex of the body as sent>'. The server mints a pairing token as for `pisa pair` and returns the pisa://pair link; the new device scans it and uses POST /v1/pair/begin and POST /v1/pair unchanged. The token counts against the 5 open tokens; {} is a valid body (name defaults to 'device'); offerId is 'offer_' and 16 random bytes, base64url. The confirming side is this phone: the server's CLI neither lists nor confirms an offered pairing. A device paired from an offer (paired_via app) never registers the first approval (Face ID) key. No signer: a signer key is host-only (E1 P1).

201.description: The offer, with its QR and typed fallback.

400.description: validation_failed: a body that does not match PairingOfferRequest, for example one carrying signer (E1 P1: a signer key is host-only, made with the CLI on the server)

404.description: the server has no TLS pin and addresses configured

x-pisa-signed-op.target: <SHA-256 hex of the request body, as sent>

post.x-pisa-signing-rule: As provider_key: once the server holds a Face ID key, a request without a valid signature for this op and target (or a nonce used twice) gets 403 biometric_required. Before the first key exists, the session token alone is enough.

get.summary: The offering phone polls its offer
get.description: Only the device that made the offer may read, withdraw or confirm it; for any other device it is 404. open until a device pairs with it (refused if withdrawn first, expired past the token's 10 minutes), then the pairing's state. At awaiting_confirmation it carries pairingId, newDevice and the transcript fields, and expiresAt is the confirmation deadline; the phone checks the reveal and computes the SAS itself (CONTRACT-2 §4.3), never trusting a SAS from the server. At confirmed, deviceId.

delete.summary: Withdraw the offer, or refuse the device that scanned it
delete.description: Unsigned: refusing grants nothing. Spends the token; a pairing awaiting confirmation becomes refused. 204 also when there is nothing left to withdraw. 404 for any device but the offering one.

post.summary: Confirm the new device after comparing the SAS
post.description: Signed: device op pairing_confirm, target '<pairingId>:<sas>', so the Face ID approval names the exact device the user compared. The server checks that the SAS it derived for that pairing equals the one sent.

200.description: confirmed, with the new device's id.

409.description: pairing_code_invalid: the pairing is not this offer's, not awaiting confirmation, or the SAS is not the server's (nothing is confirmed)

post.x-pisa-signing-rule: As provider_key: once the server holds a Face ID key, a request without a valid signature for this op and target (or a nonce used twice) gets 403 biometric_required. Before the first key exists, the session token alone is enough.

get.summary: A sheet as a Ring 1 surface
get.description: Returns the surface's A2UI operations and its pisa block instead of a v1 present object.

200.description: The same content as the activity.

sessionToken.description: The 1 h session token from POST /v1/devices/session.

XPisaNonce.name: X-Pisa-Nonce
XPisaNonce.description: A device challenge's nonce (single use, 5 minutes).

XPisaSignature.name: X-Pisa-Signature
XPisaSignature.description: The Face ID key's signature over the pisa-device canonical text: DER, base64.

name.description: A label for the new device; 'device' when absent

PairingOfferRequest.description: Closed: there is no signer field. A signer key is host-only, made with the CLI on the server (E1 P1); a body carrying signer is 400 validation_failed.

transcript.description: awaiting_confirmation only: what the phone needs to compute the SAS. The phone checks serverNonce against the commitment (as the new device does) before showing digits.

DeviceChallengeRequest.description: A signed device op (v1 CORE-SEC). The server puts the target on one line: control characters become spaces.

canonical.description: pisa-approval/2 (§6.2), or pisa-device for a device op.

id.description: The provider part of its models' references (<id>:<model id>).

ca_bundle.description: An absolute path, on the PISA server, to the PEM file of a private CA that signs the model server's certificate.

ServerUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change; ca_bundle null removes the bundle.

editable.description: false for built-in providers and for a server the operator set in the environment

Provider.description: v1's provider entry, plus the model-server fields. Further fields may appear (v1's list).

ProviderCapabilities.description: Effective capabilities (the probe with the overrides applied). An unprobed model reports every capability false, with probed_at null.

Error.description: v1's error envelope (protocol/openapi.json). 401 device_revoked: the app wipes itself (§4.5); 403 ai_consent_required (§4.4).
